meta.title: Fourier-series synthesiser: square and sawtooth waves
meta.tools: Analytic Fourier coefficients, partial-sum synthesis, RMS error predicted from the omitted harmonics (Parseval), audio (WAV) output
meta.summary: Synthesise square and sawtooth waves from their harmonics, predict the mean-square error of every partial sum from the energy in the omitted terms, and render the results as audio so the harmonic build-up can be heard.
meta.problem: How many harmonics does a square wave need — and can we predict the approximation error before computing it?
meta.theory:
Square (±1): $\frac4π\sum_{k\,odd}\frac{\sin kωt}{k}$; sawtooth: $\frac2π\sum_k\frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k}\sin kωt$. By Parseval the mean-square error of the N-harmonic partial sum equals the energy of the
omitted terms: square $\frac{8}{π^2}\sum_{k>N,\,odd}\frac1{k^2}$, sawtooth $\frac{2}{π^2}\sum_{k>N}\frac1{k^2}$ — both fall as 1/N, i.e. RMS error ∝ N^{−1/2}.
meta.method: One period sampled at 2¹⁶ points; partial sums N = 1 … 200 harmonics; measured MSE vs the tail-sum prediction. 220 Hz tones with 1, 3, 9, 27 harmonics written to a 48 kHz WAV.
meta.track: Applied Mathematics — 218 projects in electrical engineering
